newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian central bank intervenes in forex market.
newsitem.headline: Croatian central bank intervenes in forex market.

text.p: The Croatian central bank said it intervened in the foreign exchange market on Tuesday, buying 14.5 million marks and $3 million to improve banks' liquidity ahead of the summer tourist season.

The bank said in a statement it bought from commercial banks 14.5 million marks at a weighted price of 3.5725 kuna per mark, and $3 million at 6.0532 kuna per dollar, supplying them with some 70 million kuna of primary money.

The central bank calculated its kuna midrate for Wednesday firmer at 3.5771 against the mark and weaker at 6.0761 against the dollar. The auction took place on Tuesday for the payment to be carried out on Thursday, a bank official told Reuters.

"The intervention was aimed at improving the liquidity of the banks towards the end of the week," the official said. "But it is also a seasonal measure that we carry out every year ahead of the tourist season."
Banks were facing liquidity problems because of tax payments due at the end of the week.

Intervention in the foreign market is the main tool of Croatian monetary policy, which targets money supply rather than exchange rates. "The aim of the intervention was improving the kuna liquidity, not manipulating the exchange rate against foreign currencies," another official said.
